AfterPowerAmountChanged.rationale: SPLIT ACROSS TWO SIM HOOKS, and the split is correct -- this is the one unit in half A where the sim's re-architecture of a single C# hook is exactly right rather than approximately right. Hook.AfterPowerAmountChanged fires from BOTH of PowerCmd's pipelines: step 23 of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json (PowerCmd.cs:153-157, a brand-new power, gated on modifiedAmount != 0) and step 33 (PowerCmd.cs:243-246, a re-stack, gated on (int)modifiedOffset != 0). The sim has a separate hook for each -- on_power_applied at cmds.py:1054 for the new-power branch and on_power_amount_changed at cmds.py:995 for the stacking branch -- and this power implements BOTH and routes them to one _maybe_draw. So a first Bash and a second Bash both draw, on both sides. All three C# guards are present: amount <= 0 (ViciousPower.cs:21 vs powers.py:1577, where the sim's delta is `existing.amount - old_amount` at cmds.py:996 and so is 0 for a Single-stack no-op -- correctly not a draw), applier == base.Owner (:21 vs powers.py:1577), and power is VulnerablePower (:21 vs powers.py:1577's name != 'vulnerable'). Note C# has NO target-side test, and neither does the sim: Vicious draws whenever its owner applies Vulnerable to anyone. Both sides also miss the Artifact case identically -- a fully blocked Vulnerable returns at cmds.py:937-938 before any notification, matching C#'s != 0 gates. Citations re-verified and renumbered 2026-08-04 (cmds.py/hooks.py functions moved; mechanism unchanged, the two stale bare `:1167` self-references were resolved to the same powers.py:1577 line they always meant).

guards.rationale: powers.py:1580 DrawCmd.draw(self.owner, self.amount). Same count, same target.

This power is the reason a missing applier= matters, and it is worth recording where it is safe. Vicious keys entirely on `applier is self.owner`, so any sim site that applies Vulnerable WITHOUT applier= is silently invisible to it. Checked the ported Vulnerable appliers: the Ironclad card Bash and its siblings pass applier=ctx.player, and monster applications pass applier=self, so no ported Vulnerable source is applier-less. Named trigger: adding a Vulnerable application that omits applier=, which would make Vicious silently stop working -- the same class of latent break as audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json's note N2.
Neither side ticks or removes it; it draws for the rest of the combat. Both agree.
